subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invocation, and before-tool-call hooks?
rationale: The requested mode would become a user-trusted security boundary, and the current execution surfaces are broader than the proposed process-global adapter flag.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then add an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for all tool execution surfaces and unchanged normal execution.

options.title: Fold into safe workflow modes
options.body: Keep the request open but block implementation until broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Keep scoped dry-runs only
options.body: Reject a global mode if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with sandboxing and continue improving command-specific preview paths.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then add an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for all tool execution surfaces and unchanged normal execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is product/security contract shape, and this handle has the strongest historical connection to the adapter, CLI, and tools.invoke surfaces.
